rules.situation: A user asks for new access to an application or role that is not privileged, administrative, finance or production
must_never: grant access without the required approval
user_guidance: Sign out and back in after approved access is granted
quotes: New access requires the application, requested role, business reason, and manager approval.
The service desk may fulfill pre-approved standard roles.
Create an `Access` ticket when approval or an owner decision is required.
a new access request is normally medium priority.

rules.situation: A user asks for privileged, administrative, finance or production access
must_never: grant privileged, administrative, finance or production access automatically
user_guidance: Sign out and back in after approved access is granted
quotes: New access requires the application, requested role, business reason, and manager approval.
Privileged, administrative, finance, and production access must be routed to the application owner and must not be granted automatically.
Create an `Access` ticket when approval or an owner decision is required.
a new access request is normally medium priority.

rules.situation: Access the user already had stops working (signs in but the application denies access)
user_guidance: Confirm you can sign in to the company identity portal
Sign out and back in
quotes: Confirm the user can sign in to the company identity portal, identify the application and requested role, check existing group membership, and ask the user to sign out and back in after approved access is granted.
Use high priority only when an existing access failure blocks a documented business-critical activity

rules.situation: The user forgot their password or the self-service reset fails
must_never: ask for or store a password
include authentication secrets in the ticket
user_guidance: Use the self-service password reset portal
quotes: Direct the user to the self-service password reset portal.
Service desk staff and automated agents must never ask for or store a password.
If self-service reset fails, create an `Identity` ticket with the error and affected username, but do not include authentication secrets.

rules.situation: The user lost or replaced the device used for MFA and needs methods reset or a new device enrolled
must_never: request, repeat, log or validate an MFA code
reset MFA methods before a human verifies identity
user_guidance: Enroll a company-approved authenticator through the identity portal
quotes: Users enroll a company-approved authenticator through the identity portal.
Never request, repeat, log, or validate an MFA code in chat or in a ticket.
Lost or replaced devices require identity verification by a human service desk agent before MFA methods are reset.

rules.situation: Repeated unexpected MFA prompts, or a reset request the user did not start
must_never: request, repeat, log or validate an MFA code
quotes: Never request, repeat, log, or validate an MFA code in chat or in a ticket.
Repeated unexpected MFA prompts or a reset request the user did not initiate must be treated as a potential security incident and routed to Security.

rules.situation: The approved VPN, remote desktop or file-transfer client fails or stays unavailable
required_fields: whether VPN, remote desktop or file transfer is affected
must_never: advise disabling endpoint protection, firewall controls, device compliance or certificate validation
user_guidance: For expired-token or authentication errors: disconnect, sign out of the client, sign in again and reconnect
For remote desktop: check the target computer is powered on and remote access is assigned
quotes: Confirm the device is company managed, has internet access, and reports as compliant.
Record the client, operating system, error, and whether the problem affects VPN, remote desktop, or file transfer.
Do not advise users to disable endpoint protection, firewall controls, device compliance, or certificate validation.
Create a `RemoteWork` ticket when the approved client remains unavailable.

rules.situation: A network drive or shared folder can't be reached or the mapping fails
required_fields: whether other folders on the same share are accessible
must_never: copy confidential file contents into a ticket
user_guidance: Confirm you are on the office network or the approved VPN
Reconnect using the published share path and refresh your sign-in
quotes: Confirm the user is connected to the office network or approved VPN.
Capture the share path, exact error, and whether other folders on the same share are accessible.
Do not copy confidential file contents into a ticket.
Create a `Network` ticket for connectivity or mapping failures.

rules.situation: Only one folder on a share is denied, or the user asks for folder-level permissions
required_fields: whether other folders on the same share are accessible
must_never: change permissions without data-owner approval
remap the whole drive
copy confidential file contents into a ticket
quotes: Capture the share path, exact error, and whether other folders on the same share are accessible.
If only one folder is denied, treat it as an access issue rather than remapping the whole drive.
Do not change permissions without data-owner approval.
Create an `Access` ticket for folder-level permission requests and identify the data owner when known.

rules.situation: Monitors or displays are not detected
user_guidance: Reconnect the dock and use the detect-displays function
quotes: For displays, confirm power, cable connection, docking-station connection, and operating-system display detection.
Record dock and monitor models if the issue remains.

rules.situation: One user can't print or their printer connection drops
must_never: instruct users to assign an IP address
user_guidance: Check you are on the correct network, the printer is online and the queue isn't paused
Clear only your own failed jobs, then reconnect the published printer
quotes: For printers, confirm the user is on the correct network, the printer is online, and the queue is not paused.
Clear only the user's failed jobs before reconnecting the published printer.
Do not instruct users to assign an IP.

rules.situation: Multiple users lose connectivity to the same printer
must_never: instruct users to assign an IP address
quotes: Do not instruct users to assign an IP.
a `Network` ticket when multiple users lose connectivity to the same printer.

rules.situation: A workplace device has a physical failure (for example a dock with no power)
quotes: Create a `Hardware` ticket for physical failures

rules.situation: A laptop battery is swollen or overheating
user_guidance: Stop using and charging the device immediately
quotes: A swollen or overheating battery requires the user to stop using and charging the device immediately.

rules.situation: An approved application is missing from the software portal
must_never: state that software is approved or licensed unless the system of record confirms it
user_guidance: Refresh the software portal once
quotes: Approved software must be installed from the company software portal.
If an approved application is missing, refresh the portal once and capture the application name, device ID, and displayed error.

rules.situation: The user asks for software that is not standard or not yet approved
must_never: state that the software is approved or licensed unless the system of record confirms it
install software outside the company software portal
quotes: For non-standard software, create a `Software` request containing the product, business reason, manager approval, and requested duration.
An automated agent must not state that software is approved or licensed unless the system of record confirms it.

rules.situation: License activation fails
must_never: place license keys in chat, logs or tickets
quotes: For activation failures, capture the product, license-server name, error code, and number of affected users.
Widespread failures may be an infrastructure incident.
Never place license keys in chat, logs, or tickets.

rules.situation: One user has a problem with email, chat, meetings or another collaboration tool
required_fields: whether sending, receiving, access or device operation is affected
user_guidance: Check the published service-status page
quotes: Identify the service, affected user or group, start time, and whether the issue affects sending, receiving, access, or device operation.
Route isolated access issues to `Communication`.

rules.situation: Multiple users can't use email, chat, meetings or another collaboration tool
required_fields: whether sending, receiving, access or device operation is affected
must_never: create a duplicate incident ticket without checking service status
quotes: Identify the service, affected user or group, start time, and whether the issue affects sending, receiving, access, or device operation.
Check the published service-status page before creating duplicate incident tickets.
If multiple users are affected and no active incident exists, create a high-priority Collaboration incident.

rules.situation: The user needs access to a channel, recording, distribution list or meeting room
quotes: Channel, recording, distribution-list, and room access may be controlled by a group owner.
New access requires the resource name and owner approval.

rules.situation: Mail delivery is intermittent
must_never: copy confidential message bodies unless required
quotes: For intermittent mail delivery, record sender, recipient, timestamp, and message ID; do not copy confidential message bodies unless required.

rules.situation: Suspected phishing, unexpected MFA prompts, malware alerts, lost devices or possible account compromise
must_never: request passwords, MFA codes, private keys, recovery codes or full payment-card data
tell the user to disable endpoint protection or delete evidence
promise that an account or device is safe
user_guidance: Stop interacting with the suspicious content
Contact the Security Hotline
quotes: For suspected phishing, unexpected MFA prompts, malware alerts, lost devices, or possible account compromise, instruct the user to stop interacting with the suspicious content and contact the Security Hotline.
Create a high-priority `Security` ticket with a concise description, affected device or account identifier, time observed, and actions already taken.
Do not request passwords, MFA codes, private keys, recovery codes, or full payment-card data.
Do not tell the user to disable endpoint protection or delete evidence.
Do not promise that an account or device is safe.
Security Operations determines containment, evidence collection, credential reset, device isolation, and closure.

rules.situation: The user asks to restore deleted or damaged data
must_never: overwrite current data when an alternate-location restore is possible
claim a restore succeeded before the restore system reports completion and the requester or data owner verifies it
quotes: Identify the system, backup policy, affected data, approximate last-known-good time, and business impact.
Create a `DataProtection` ticket with restore scope, target location, requested restore point, data owner, and approval when required.
Restore into an alternate location when possible to avoid overwriting current data.
Do not claim a restore succeeded until the restore system reports completion and the requester or data owner verifies the result.

rules.situation: The user wants to confirm data is backed up, or a backup job succeeded but a file seems missing
must_never: treat a successful backup job as proof that every file can be restored
quotes: Identify the system, backup policy, affected data, approximate last-known-good time, and business impact.
A successful job status confirms that a backup ran; it does not by itself prove every file can be restored.

rules.situation: A virtual desktop (VDI) or enterprise application is slow, freezes or performs badly
must_never: recommend repeated restarts, registry changes, disabling security software or increasing resources without evidence
user_guidance: Save your work and reconnect once
Compare from another approved network if practical
quotes: Record the service, user impact, start time, frequency, device and network, region, error, and whether other users are affected.
For VDI, capture the session or pool identifier.
Check service status before opening an incident.
Ask the user to save work and reconnect once.
Do not recommend repeated restarts, registry changes, disabling security software, or increasing resources without evidence.
Create a `Performance` ticket for an isolated reproducible problem.

rules.situation: Any issue affecting several users or a shared service
must_never: create a duplicate incident when an active incident matches
mark an incident resolved because one user recovers
user_guidance: Give the user the matching incident's public status
quotes: Before creating an incident for a shared-service problem, check the current service-status feed and search open tickets for the same service, symptom, location, and time window.
If an active incident already matches, link the request to that incident and provide its public status; do not create a duplicate incident.
If there is no match and multiple users are affected, create a high-priority incident with the affected service, scope, start time, and observed symptoms.
Do not mark an incident resolved because one user recovers.

rules.situation: Any security case or physical safety hazard
user_guidance: Give the immediate steps from the relevant article now
Ask for missing details in a follow-up message
quotes: Security and safety cases must not wait for missing details.
Create the ticket at once with the information available, give the user the immediate steps from the relevant article, and flag the ticket for immediate staff review.
Ask for any missing details in a follow-up message.
Security cases include suspected phishing, unexpected MFA prompts, malware alerts, lost or stolen devices and possible account compromise (KB-002, KB-008).
Safety cases include a swollen or overheating battery (KB-005).
